title: fields: an html or richtext cell may still draw a stored heading at full size in a list row
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36344 (PR #36428, a markdown heading in a list cell draws at the cell's text size). The dev noted it from the code, not measured; the landing record carried it unfiled. Filed by the seat.

## What happens (read from the code, to be measured)

#36428 gave `MarkdownContent` a cell face, so a markdown heading in a grid cell draws as a paragraph at the cell's size. An `html` or `richtext` field's cell goes through `HtmlCellRenderer`, which has no cell face. A stored `h1` there probably still draws as a heading and makes the row taller than the grid's one-line clamp.

## To do

1. Measure it: render an `html` and a `richtext` value holding an `h1` through `ObjectGrid`, and record the row height and whether `tbody` holds a heading element.
2. If it does, give the html cell the same face #36428 gave markdown: heading levels drawn as `p.font-semibold` at the cell's font size, sanitisation unchanged.
3. Keep the record page and readonly form fields on their full-size headings, pinned as #36428 pins them.

## Acceptance

- In a list, an `html` or `richtext` cell holding a heading stays one line at the cell's text size, and the record page still shows the heading at full size.

## Grade
p3 · area:ux · domain:ui. Possible row-height defect, not yet measured.
